title: Mouse Without Borders vertical layout fails without mouse wrapping

status.label: Compare vertical matrix persistence
status.detail: Reporter supplied steps, a recording and a legacy-UI workaround; related tracking work is not a fix.

next_action.label: Compare modern and legacy layout values
next_action.reason: A working legacy editor helps distinguish settings serialization from runtime neighbor traversal.

judgment.rationale: The same vertical arrangement works through the original UI, making a modern-editor matrix mismatch more plausible than a blanket unsupported-topology explanation.
evidence: 0.73.0/0.74 reports disable single-row layout and wrapping, then observe one-way vertical failure or layout reset.
https://github.com/microsoft/PowerToys/issues/28757#issuecomment-1766502716 reports the original UI workaround; a later commenter confirms it works.
MouseWithoutBordersPage.Device_Drop swaps indexed devices; the view model maintains a four-slot matrix and MatrixOneRow.
MachineStuff.MoveUp/MoveDown gate vertical traversal on MatrixOneRow and use LiveMachineMatrix.
Related open reports #41449 and tracker #51077 do not provide a concrete implementation.
judgment.recommended_action: Reproduce with two physical PCs, compare the persisted four-slot matrices from each editor, and fix the first demonstrated divergence.

fix_assessment.rationale: A layout mapping or synchronization fix is plausible; the reviewed related reports and tracker do not cover it with an existing fix.

proposed_fixes.title: Preserve vertical device slots consistently between editor and runtime
proposed_fixes.root_cause: Hypothesis: the modern editor's indexed four-slot matrix or synchronization normalizes vertical layouts differently from the legacy editor, so the runtime receives incorrect neighbor slots or a one-row flag.
plan: Compare the exact four-slot matrix, MatrixOneRow and wrapping flags produced by both editors for both top/bottom orientations.

Trace Device_Drop and LoadMachineMatrixString in the Settings view/view model and LiveMachineMatrix/MoveUp/MoveDown in MachineStuff.cs; distinguish elevation-disabled drag behavior from a saved-layout mismatch.
Correct the demonstrated slot-mapping or synchronization divergence without compacting intentional empty slots; if saved matrices match, investigate runtime neighbor traversal instead.
Add round-trip tests for empty matrix slots, reversed vertical order, disconnected/reconnected peers and wrap enabled/disabled.
verification: Two physical PCs can cross the shared vertical edge in both directions without wrapping; nonadjacent outer edges do not wrap.
Modern and legacy editors produce equivalent runtime topology, which survives Settings reopen and PowerToys restart.

confidence.rationale: The working legacy-editor comparison is strong discrimination, but no actual settings diff or physical two-PC test was performed.

issue_context.summary: A two-PC vertical layout either resets in the modern editor or cannot be traversed without wrapping; configuring it in the original UI is a reported workaround.
known_information: The report gives exact single-row/wrapping settings and both vertical orientations.
The author retested 0.74 and supplied a recording.
Two commenters report success using the original UI; the latest also asks about a more complex multi-monitor topology.
inferences: The original-UI workaround suggests editor/matrix consistency should be tested first, but does not prove a serialization bug.
The later request to choose an individual monitor is a separate scope from the two-device vertical regression.
issue_context.analysis: The available workaround enables a targeted maintainer experiment. Do not ask the reporter to repeat supplied settings or claim tracker #51077 implements a fix.
initial_investigation: Read the complete report and three comments; checked #41449, #51077, timeline and related PR search.
Inspected Device_Drop, LoadMachineMatrixString, MatrixOneRow and the runtime vertical-neighbor gates in upstream source.

actions.label: Compare vertical layouts from both editors

reproduce.version: Current stable build; report confirmed on 0.73.0 and 0.74
prerequisites: Two connected physical PCs; record elevation because modern UI drag is disabled when elevated.
steps: Arrange PC A above PC B in the modern editor, then test upward and downward crossing.
Reverse top/bottom order and repeat, noting any reset to horizontal.
Configure the same topology in the original UI when available and repeat.
Compare the four machine slots, single-row and wrapping values on both peers before and after reopening Settings.
Trace the first differing editor/runtime value, then repeat with wrapping enabled as a control.
reproduce.expected_result: Both vertical arrangements persist, and crossing occurs only at the shared edge with wrapping disabled.

actions.label: Approve vertical-matrix consistency plan
actions.note: Use the modern/legacy comparison to select the actual failing layer before implementation.
